definition: A pan turned left or right so fast that the image blurs.
example: We reveal the next person with a whip pan.

definition: A move where the camera itself gets closer to the subject.
example: We dolly in to match the expression.

definition: A move where the camera itself moves away from the subject.
example: We dolly out to reveal the space.

definition: Making the subject appear larger in frame by increasing the focal length.
example: Zoom in on the sign.

definition: Capturing a wider range in frame by decreasing the focal length.
example: Zoom out so the surroundings are visible.

definition: A technique that changes perspective by combining camera movement with a zoom in the opposite direction.
example: We use a dolly zoom at the uneasy moment.

definition: Rotating the camera around the axis pointing toward the lens.
example: Give it a tilting feel with a roll.
note: On set, 'roll camera' is a cue to start recording, a different usage from the camera rotation described here.

definition: A shot that moves in an arc around the subject.
example: We capture the two people with an arc shot around them.

definition: A shot in which the camera's position and framing do not move.
example: This scene is a fixed shot.

definition: A move that raises or lowers the entire camera vertically.
example: We match eye level with a pedestal up.

definition: A move where the camera travels sideways in parallel.
example: We truck right alongside the subject.

definition: A shot that moves the camera up and down with a crane or jib arm.
example: We reveal the yard with a boom up.

definition: A method of shooting while supporting the camera with the hands or shoulder.
example: We'll go handheld for the moving scene.
note: 'Demochi' is a field term found in 1985 language-refinement materials.

definition: Equipment that supports the camera on three legs.
example: We put the camera on the tripod.

definition: A wheeled support rig that carries the camera and moves it smoothly.
example: We check the dolly's path of movement.

definition: Equipment that moves the camera a short distance along a rail.
example: We push the slider past the product.

definition: Equipment that mounts the camera on a long arm for wide movement.
example: We capture the whole stage with a jib.
note: 'Jimmy Jib' is a field term derived from an equipment brand name. Not every jib is a product of that brand.

definition: A name for a body-mounted stabilizer class used for smooth moving shots.
example: We follow the hallway with a Steadicam.
note: Steadicam is an equipment brand name. Don't confuse it as a generic term for all stabilizers or electronic gimbals.

definition: A stabilizer that reduces camera shake by controlling rotation axes.
example: Balance the gimbal first.

definition: A device that fixes the camera to an actor's body so it moves with them.
example: We fix the figure in place and show them with a Snorricam.

definition: A lens with a single fixed focal length.
example: Today we use a 50mm prime lens.

definition: A lens whose focal length can be changed.
example: We adjust the composition with a zoom lens.

definition: A short-focal-length lens that captures a wide angle of view on the same sensor.
example: We capture the narrow interior with a wide-angle lens.

definition: A long-focal-length lens that captures distant subjects large.
example: We shoot the distant stage with a telephoto lens.

definition: A lens with a focal length near the diagonal length of the sensor.
example: We check the composition with a standard lens.

definition: A lens designed to capture small subjects large from close up.
example: We shoot texture with a macro lens.

definition: A lens property where set focus is maintained even when the zoom changes.
example: Check that it's parfocal before zooming.

definition: A lens method that records the image horizontally compressed and expands it later.
example: We expand the image to match the anamorphic.

definition: A technique that shifts focus to subjects at different distances within one shot.
example: We rack focus from the cup to the figure.

definition: A camera assistant who sets and maintains focus during shooting.
example: We coordinate movement with the focus puller.

definition: A device that helps precisely control lens focus.
example: We mark distances on the follow focus.

definition: A state where the in-focus front-to-back range is narrow.
example: We emphasize the figure with a shallow depth of field.
note: 'Out-focusing' is linked as a search term for the effect of blurring the background. Distinguish it from a state where the entire image is out of focus.

definition: A state where everything appears sharp from near to far.
example: We show the space with a deep depth of field.

definition: The main light that illuminates the subject.
example: Place the key light on the left.

definition: Light that softens the shadows created by the key light.
example: Reduce the fill light a little.

definition: Light shone from behind the subject to separate it from the background.
example: We separate the figure with a back light.

definition: Light that creates a bright outline along the edge of the subject.
example: Add a rim light on the shoulder.

definition: A lighting source that is actually visible within the frame.
example: We use the lamp as a practical.

definition: Light reflected off a wall or reflector.
example: We soften it with a ceiling bounce.

definition: Light that creates sharply defined shadows.
example: We bring out texture with hard light.

definition: Light that creates soft-edged shadows.
example: We light the face with soft light.

definition: An opaque board or cloth that blocks light or limits its spread.
example: We block the light on the wall with a flag.

definition: Flaps in front of a light that control the spread of the beam.
example: We reduce the side light with barn doors.

definition: A basic lighting setup combining key, fill, and back light.
example: We start the interview with three-point lighting.

definition: A lighting style that keeps a bright tone with little contrast.
example: It's a bright commercial, so we go high key.

definition: A lighting style that uses dark areas and strong contrast.
example: We create tension with low key.

definition: Material or treatment that scatters light to make it soft.
example: We install diffusion on the window.

definition: A method that absorbs or blocks reflected light to deepen shadows.
example: We add negative fill with black cloth.

definition: Brightness control related to the amount of light reaching the sensor.
example: We check exposure against the view outside the window.

definition: The part inside a lens that adjusts the size of the opening light passes through.
example: We stop down the aperture to increase depth of field.

definition: The time light is received when recording a single frame.
example: We adjust the shutter to match the motion.

definition: A sensitivity setting that affects image brightness processing and noise.
example: We check the lighting and ISO together.

definition: A state recorded brighter than needed, where detail in bright areas may be lost.
example: We check the sky for overexposure.

definition: A state recorded darker than needed, where dark areas are hard to distinguish.
example: We compensate for underexposure on the face.

definition: An edit that lets the next scene's sound be heard before the picture.
example: We let the next line be heard first with a J-cut.

definition: An edit where the previous scene's sound continues after the picture changes.
example: We show the reaction with an L-cut.

definition: An edit where the transition points of sound and picture differ.
example: We connect the dialogue with a split edit.

definition: An edit that cuts within a similar composition so that time or action appears to jump.
example: We shorten the pause with a jump cut.

definition: An edit that joins different shots using similarity of form, action, or sound.
example: We connect round shapes with a match cut.

definition: A single piece of video or audio used in editing.
example: We place the clip on the timeline.

definition: A single still image that makes up a video.
example: We check frame by frame.

definition: The number of frames recorded or played per second.
example: We match the frame rate.

definition: A method or program that compresses and restores video and audio.
example: We check the delivery codec.

definition: The process of computing the result of edits and effects into a final image.
example: We render the effect section.

definition: A technique that makes a specific color range transparent to composite it with another image.
example: We key out the green background with chroma key.

definition: An animation reference point that specifies a property value at a specific time.
example: We add a keyframe to the position.

definition: The bands left at the top and bottom when maintaining an aspect ratio.
example: We match the ratio without letterboxing.

definition: An edit assembling the main flow before detailed refinement.
example: We check the structure in the rough cut.

definition: The location's inherent background sound, recorded without dialogue or action.
example: We record this room's room tone.

definition: A small microphone attached to clothing or the body.
example: We check the lavalier for clothing rustle.

definition: A long directional microphone designed to pick up sound mainly from the front.
example: We point the shotgun toward the speaker.

definition: A long pole for placing the mic near the speaker from off-frame.
example: Keep the boom pole out of the frame.

definition: DC power supplied through the microphone cable.
example: We check the mic's phantom power requirement.
note: The required voltage and support vary by microphone and input device. It is not a feature that must be turned on for every microphone.

definition: The stage of planning, casting, and preparation before the main shoot.
example: We set the blocking in pre-production.

definition: The production stage of actually shooting the planned scenes.
example: The production schedule begins.

definition: The stage of completing editing, color, and sound after shooting.
example: We set the post-production schedule.

definition: A document announcing the day's shooting schedule, locations, participants, and more.
example: We check tomorrow's call sheet.

definition: The designated time by which shooting participants must arrive on set.
example: The call time differs by team.

definition: The task of setting the positions and movements of actors in a scene.
example: We move the camera to match the blocking.

definition: An instruction to start camera recording.
example: Roll camera—we're ready.

definition: An instruction to start audio recording.
example: We wait for the cue after roll sound.

definition: The cue to begin the actors' performance and movement.
example: Open the door after action.

definition: The signal to stop the ongoing performance and shooting.
example: Cut—let's reset the blocking.

definition: A plan that organizes the order and composition of shots as drawings.
example: We align the flow with the storyboard.

definition: Review footage for checking the day's shoot.
example: We check continuity in the dailies.

definition: A shooting backdrop where the boundary of wall and floor is joined by a curved surface.
example: We shoot the product on the cyclorama.
note: The cyclorama from English-language sources is linked to the domestic term for a shooting backdrop. The specific spatial form varies by studio.

definition: The work of creating and recording action sounds directly in post to match the picture.
example: We supplement the footsteps with Foley.

definition: A shot that briefly turns attention to another subject or reaction from the main action.
example: We insert a cutaway of the listener.

definition: A shooting and grading method that makes scenes shot in daytime look like night.
example: We test day for night.

definition: The work of adjusting exposure, color balance, and such to set the image's baseline color.
example: We match color correction across cameras.

definition: The work of designing color and contrast for a scene's emotion and mood.
example: We give it a cold mood with grading.

definition: A display that checks image signal brightness and such as a waveform.
example: We check brightness with the waveform.

definition: A conversion table that changes input color values into set output values.
example: We apply a LUT suited to the source.
note: Uses differ, from technical color-space conversion to creative color application. Check which camera or color space it's for.

definition: A shooting method that records brightness information along a log curve.
example: We apply a conversion suited to the log footage.
note: Log is not the same as RAW. It needs conversion matched to the recording curve and the camera's color space.

definition: A technical role that manages the color, signal, and workflow of digital footage on set.
example: We check monitor color with the DIT.

definition: A board that records shot information and marks a reference for syncing sound and picture.
example: We check the slate number.

definition: Aligning the timing of separately recorded sound and picture.
example: We sync using the slate.

definition: A marking that no sound is recorded for that footage.
example: We shoot this insert MOS.
note: There are several theories about the origin of the abbreviation, so we don't assert one. Here we describe only its actual use as a silent-shooting marking.

definition: The person who records and checks takes and scene continuity.
example: The script supervisor checks continuity.

definition: A method of slating at the end of a take instead of the start.
example: This time we record it with a tail slate.

definition: A notice that the slate will be clapped gently.
example: The face is close, so let's go with soft sticks.
note: A cue found in English-language on-set materials. Not every domestic set uses the same term.

definition: A signal that the slate will be clapped again.
example: The sound was faint, so we go with second sticks.
note: A cue found in English-language on-set materials. Domestically it may be said as 'slate again' and such.

definition: An edit that adjusts a clip's length while pushing or pulling the following clips along.
example: We close the gap with a ripple edit.

definition: An edit that moves the boundary of two adjoining clips while keeping the total length.
example: We move the transition point with a rolling edit.

definition: An edit that keeps a clip's position and length while changing its internal start and end frames.
example: We change the expression with a slip edit.

definition: An edit that moves a clip and adjusts adjacent clip lengths to keep the total length.
example: We move the position with a slide edit.

definition: The work of refining a clip's in and out points.
example: We trim the part where they catch their breath.

definition: An expression for preparing and taking care of things so work goes smoothly.
example: We check the groundwork before the event.

definition: A term for a flaw or scratch mark on the surface of an object.
example: We check whether there are scratches on the panel.

definition: An expression used to mean full or to the fullest.
example: My schedule is packed today, so it's hard to add another meeting.
note: It can be replaced with specific words like 'full' or 'to the maximum'. If it's an instruction to adjust equipment, check the exact value.

definition: A field term for a cart used to move loads.
example: We move the boxes with a cart.

definition: Arranging elements to a consistent reference line.
example: We left-align the title.

definition: Information that describes in words what an image conveys.
example: We add alt text to the photo.

definition: The ratio of a screen's width to its height.
example: We set the aspect ratio to 16:9.

definition: The reference line in typography on which letters sit.
example: We align the body text baseline.

definition: Operations that create shapes by uniting, subtracting, or intersecting shapes.
example: We cut a hole with a Boolean operation.

definition: A mathematical curve whose shape is controlled by control points.
example: We refine the outline with a Bézier curve.

definition: The actual text that goes into a design, such as titles and body.
example: We shorten the button copy.

definition: The part of a lowercase letter that rises above the x-height.
example: It's a typeface with long ascenders.

definition: The degree to which people of varying abilities and environments can use a product.
example: We check keyboard accessibility.
